own_scenes.family: Costa Oeste: Los Ángeles, Compton, la Bahía
own_scenes.desc: Las cintas del hip hop llegaban a la Costa Oeste con los familiares y los soldados; allí, entre la herencia de los disturbios de Watts (1965) y el «blockbusting» que convirtió Compton en una ciudad negra, la escena de DJs móviles se volcó en Bambaataa y la electrónica. Alonzo Williams, antes Disco Lonzo, dirigió el Eve After Dark desde 1979 con concursos de baile y rap (Ice-T ganó uno con Kurtis Blow de jurado) y formó la World Class Wreckin’ Cru, grupo de electro-rap con trajes de lentejuelas: DJ Yella, Cli-N-Tel y Dr. Dre, vecino suyo que mezclaba «Please Mr. Postman» con un break. Davy DMX, el DJ de Kurtis Blow, enseñó a Yella, Yella a Dre y Dre a los demás; «Slice» y «Surgery» salieron en Kru-Cut y Macola antes de fichar por CBS/Epic. Su rival, el Uncle Jamm’s Army de Rodger Clayton y Gid Martin, juntaba a diez mil chavales en el Sports Arena solo con DJs y crió a Ice-T, DJ Pooh y Egyptian Lover; se arrancaban los carteles a cinco dólares la pieza. En el club Radio (luego Radiotron), más club punk que otra cosa, Chris «The Glove» Taylor, que scratcheaba «como un batería», puso la música de Breakin’ (1984) y produjo con Ice-T «Reckless».

refs.q: The East Coast and the West Coast are completely different nations at this time.
refs.para: Chris “The Glove” Taylor (DJ, producer): The East Coast and the West Coast are completely different nations at this time. Records took forever to migrate across the United States. So, I get my hands on a record called “The Adventures of Grandmaster Flash on the Wheels of Steel.” I’m hearing these sounds. Turns out, it’s scratching. I had no idea of what this was, but I was just into it.

refs.q: When hip-hop finally took root on the West Coast, I was the one that dug the hole for the root.
refs.para: Alonzo Williams (DJ, World Class Wreckin’ Cru): When we first opened the Eve, hip-hop was not really in existence on the West Coast, not at all. When hip-hop finally took root on the West Coast, I was the one that dug the hole for the root.

refs.q: Because he taught Yella, and then Yella taught Dre and subsequently me, and Joe Cooley.
refs.para: Cli-N-Tel (artist, World Class Wreckin’ Cru): As DJs on the West Coast, we started watching DJ Yella, so in essence Davy DMX taught all of us. Because he taught Yella, and then Yella taught Dre and subsequently me, and Joe Cooley. We just started watching Yella and studying him and that’s how we learned.

refs.q: Rodger looked at the crowd, pointed to all those kids, and he says, “Does it look like I need fucking radio?”
refs.para: I immediately decided that if those guys have that kind of control in the streets, I want to be a part of that. I met with Rodger Clayton and I asked him if we could tie in with it. Rodger looked at the crowd, pointed to all those kids, and he says, “Does it look like I need fucking radio?”
